scope: All20 ops/ entries of root_integration_ops-files.json; read only, no historical operator or qualification script execution.

checks.detail: record140/150/160 pin both source checkouts, launchers, binary, rollback CHECK and empty rollback runtime log before bounded checkpoint parse. Exact prior identity and existing section digest gate all changes. Deep copies preserve every unknown/historical block; prior active is archived separately from compatible rollback; no legal/backup/PC/runtime evidence inferred. Exclusive flock on source inode, fingerprint/bytes recheck, private temporary file/fsync/replace/readback and retry read-only semantics reviewed.

checks.name: synthetic_tests
checks.detail: All9 synthetic Python files included in20-file coverage. They substitute in-memory pins or tempfile-owned fixture paths/modules, verify wrong identities/hashes/modes/links/partial artifacts, checkpoint preservation/idempotence, precheck and SQL unknown outcomes, TTY private input. This audit neither re-ran them nor claimed their old passing outputs certify current182 host state.

limits: No new claim of production runtime readiness, SQL state, Manager stop/start, hosted CHECK, backup or PC qualification. None of the20 files was executed by this reviewer; shell snippets, embedded Python/JS and test harnesses were read statically only.
Historical1.4/1.5/1.6 operators are not current182 commands. SQL36 and the current182 checkpoint remain authoritative. A successful historical fixture does not authorize replay on production.

Metadata writers document a pre-replace drift check, not a universal filesystem compare-and-swap; same-operator hostile concurrent path replacement and compromised operator environment are not certified as isolated. No concrete remote attack path through these dormant helpers was identified.
The20 files exclude current181/182 tools/workflows and every non-ops root-manifest entry; these retain the parent owner. This report does not assert coverage of those excluded files.

A complete direct source read was used for family bases; variant coverage was complete base plus exhaustive unfiltered diff, recorded explicitly rather than claimed as a separate direct cat of every variant.
